title: All four 'held-out' boards in the Hill promotion gate are registered live blend sources, so the benchmark is not independent of the board it grades
subsystem: Model registry / Hill curve promotion gate
claimUnderTest: holdout.py: 'this module evaluates the curve against value-publishing markets that the fit never sees' and CLAUDE.md: the refit 'scores it against dynasty boards the fit never reads'. The word held-out is used throughout to mean independent.
observed: OFFENSE_HOLDOUT_SOURCES = {FantasyCalc, OTCFFB, PFKDynasty, FantasyNavigator}. All four resolve to _SOURCE_CSV_PATHS keys fantasyCalc / otcffbSf / pfkDynasty / fantasyNavigatorSf, and all four are entries in _RANKING_SOURCES with weight 1.0 and scope overall_offense — i.e. voting members of the live blend the curve produces. Five of the six TRAINING sources are also live blend sources. There is not one board on either side of the split that sits outside the pipeline. holdout.py's own guard reasons about this exact failure mode (it excludes ktcSfTep because it 'would smuggle a training source back in under a different filename') but only guards label/path collisions between train and holdout, never membership in the blend. Worse: fantasyNavigatorSf carries correlation_group='ktc' with the registry comment 'republishes KTC-derived numbers, so the two are not independent votes' — KTC is a TRAINING source, so a documented KTC derivative sits in the holdout set.

reproduction.command: cd /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket && .venv/bin/python -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'.');import src.api.data_contract as dc;from src.model_registry import holdout;reg={s['key'] for s in dc._RANKING_SOURCES};cfg=dc._SOURCE_CSV_PATHS;f=lambda p:[k for k,v in cfg.items() if isinstance(v,dict) and v.get('path')==p];print([(l,f(p)[0] in reg) for l,(p,_c) in holdout.OFFENSE_HOLDOUT_SOURCES.items()])"
reproduction.expected: holdout boards absent from the live blend registry

userImpact: Nothing a user sees changes today, but every future curve promotion is decided by a criterion that measures agreement with markets already averaged into the answer. A curve that drifts toward the crowd scores better on the gate and simultaneously becomes more redundant with the blend's own inputs — the gate cannot detect the failure it exists to catch.

priorFinding.note: Independently reproduced at runtime against the live _RANKING_SOURCES registry. Adds the fantasyNavigatorSf/KTC correlation-group leg, which the prior finding did not name.

whatWorks: holdout.py DOES refuse to score when train and holdout overlap by label or by CSV path, and raises rather than degrading to a passing score when no board can be scored. Its _semantics block states plainly that it does not measure accuracy.
rootCause: 'Held out' was defined relative to the FIT, not relative to the SYSTEM. Every value-publishing dynasty board the repo can reach was already recruited into the blend, so no genuinely external benchmark was left to hold out.
requiredRepair: Either (a) remove the four boards from _RANKING_SOURCES and reserve them permanently as the benchmark, accepting a 17-source blend, or (b) keep them in the blend and rename the criterion to what it measures — cross-market shape agreement — and stop describing promotion as validation.

title: The promotion gate scores the Hill curve against the exact value columns the live pipeline throws away — all four holdout boards are rank-signal sources demoted for having the wrong value decay
subsystem: Model registry / Hill curve promotion gate
claimUnderTest: promotion.py: 'a promotion means the challenger generalizes better across held-out dynasty markets'. The implied object of generalization is the thing the pipeline consumes from those markets.
observed: holdout.py loads each holdout board's `value` column and computes RMSE of the Hill curve against its normalized value decay. But dc.rank_signal_source_keys() contains all four of fantasyCalc, otcffbSf, fantasyNavigatorSf, pfkDynasty — the live blend reads only their ORDINAL RANK and synthesizes a value by pushing that rank through the Hill curve. Their published values never enter the board. The registry comments record why: fantasyCalc and otcffbSf were value-direct until 2026-07-25 and were switched to rank-signal precisely because their value decay was too steep against the consensus (Hampel-flagged 54.9%->58% and 55.6%->86% of rows respectively, 'four of every five of its votes were discarded'). So the gate now rewards the champion curve for reproducing decay shapes the pipeline formally rejected as unusable, on boards whose values it deletes.

reproduction.command: cd /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket && .venv/bin/python -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'.');import src.api.data_contract as dc;from src.model_registry import holdout;rs=dc.rank_signal_source_keys();cfg=dc._SOURCE_CSV_PATHS;f=lambda p:[k for k,v in cfg.items() if isinstance(v,dict) and v.get('path')==p];print({l:(col,f(p)[0] in rs) for l,(p,col) in holdout.OFFENSE_HOLDOUT_SOURCES.items()})"
reproduction.expected: holdout boards whose value columns the blend actually consumes
reproduction.actual: {'FantasyCalc': ('value', True), 'OTCFFB': ('value', True), 'PFKDynasty': ('value', True), 'FantasyNavigator': ('value', True)} — all four scored on `value`, all four rank-signal in the blend

numericProof.formula: count(holdout boards whose scored column is read by _compute_unified_rankings)

userImpact: The curve that prices every player on /rankings is tuned to match value distributions the same codebase declared systematically wrong. A promotion driven by this criterion moves the whole board toward a decay shape the Hampel filter would eject if it arrived as a vote.

priorFinding.note: Reproduced from the live registry; the demotion rationale is quoted verbatim from _SOURCE_CSV_PATHS comments at data_contract.py:351-410.

whatWorks: The rank-signal conversion itself is well-evidenced and documented with before/after Hampel rates.
rootCause: The holdout set was chosen when the four boards were value-direct and never revisited when three months later they were all switched to rank-signal.
requiredRepair: Score the gate on the quantity the pipeline actually uses (rank ordering — e.g. Spearman of the curve-implied order against the board's order), or restrict the holdout to boards whose values the blend consumes value-direct. Neither is possible today without first fixing W04-F001.

title: Six of the eight Hill constants a promotion ships have no out-of-sample score at all — the 2026-07-29 promotion shipped a −34.6% IDP curve change on the strength of an offense-only ±4.8% verdict
subsystem: Model registry / Hill curve promotion gate
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'It produces a challenger, scores it against dynasty boards the fit never reads, records the verdict.' Read naturally, the challenger is the parameter set.
observed: A ModelVersion carries all eight CONSTANT_NAMES and `apply` writes all eight. But evaluate_offense_master() takes exactly (c, s) and the registry's holdout.params for champion v2 is {'c': 0.11, 's': 1.11} — the OFFENSE pair only. hill_masters.py names this honestly (VALIDATED_PARAMS = HILL_PERCENTILE_C/S, 'only these two of the eight have a genuine out-of-sample check today'), but that honesty does not reach the version-level `qualified: true` flag, the `confidence: measured` label, `status` output, or CLAUDE.md. The v1→v2 promotion of 2026-07-29 therefore shipped, unscored: HILL_GLOBAL_PERCENTILE_S 0.87→0.725, IDP_HILL_PERCENTILE_C/S 0.093/0.97→0.083/1.11, HILL_ROOKIE 0.128/0.865→0.153/0.885.

reproduction.command: cd /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket && .venv/bin/python -c "import sys,json;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from src.model_registry.versioning import ModelRegistry;from src.model_registry.hill_masters import VALIDATED_PARAMS,CONSTANT_NAMES;r=ModelRegistry.load('hill_scope_masters');v=r.champion;print('shipped:',len(CONSTANT_NAMES),'scored:',v.holdout['params'],'validated:',VALIDATED_PARAMS,'qualified:',v.qualified,'confidence:',v.confidence)"
reproduction.expected: the scored parameter set equals the shipped parameter set
reproduction.actual: shipped: 8 · scored: {'c': 0.11, 's': 1.11} · validated: ('HILL_PERCENTILE_C','HILL_PERCENTILE_S') · qualified: True · confidence: measured

userImpact: Every IDP value on /rankings and in every trade engine moved by up to −34.6% (−23.9% at rank 200, −15.0% at rank 100) in a change whose only evidence was an offense-board RMSE. An IDP-heavy roster was repriced against no measurement, and the payload labels the champion `confidence: measured`.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed and quantified: the prior finding states the 6-of-8 ratio; this adds the per-rank curve deltas that make the size of the unscored change concrete.

whatWorks: hill_masters.VALIDATED_PARAMS is an explicit, correct in-code admission of exactly this gap.
rootCause: evaluate_offense_master is the only scorer that was ever written; the version/promotion machinery was built to carry a whole parameter set and no one narrowed the verdict to what it covers.
requiredRepair: Either build GLOBAL/IDP scorers over their own held-out boards, or split the registry so a promotion moves only HILL_PERCENTILE_C/S and the other six require a separate explicit human decision. At minimum, ModelVersion.qualified/confidence must be per-parameter, not per-version.

title: The IDP Hill master is fit from two sources that never evaluate it and applied to four that never trained it — the overlap between its training set and its application set is exactly zero
claimUnderTest: player_valuation.py: 'IDP master — fit from IDPTradeCalc's IDP slice (the only value-based IDP source). Used for every IDP-scope source's contributions.'
observed: The IDP master is fit from IDPTradeCalc's IDP slice plus DraftSharks-IDP. Neither consumes it: idpTradeCalc is in _VALUE_BASED_SOURCES so it votes value-direct (raw/site_max×9999) and touches no Hill curve, and draftSharksIdp carries is_cross_market=True so _curve_for_source routes it to the GLOBAL master. The IDP master is applied to dlfIdp, dlfRookieIdp, idpShow, fantasyProsIdp — four rank-signal sources that publish no values at all and therefore contributed nothing to the fit. Set intersection of {fit} and {applied} is empty.

reproduction.command: cd /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket && .venv/bin/python -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'.');import src.api.data_contract as dc;V=set(dc._VALUE_BASED_SOURCES);I=dc.SOURCE_SCOPE_OVERALL_IDP;print('IDP-curve-routed:',[s['key'] for s in dc._RANKING_SOURCES if s['key'] not in V and not s.get('is_cross_market') and str(s.get('scope'))==I]);print('idpTradeCalc value-direct:', 'idpTradeCalc' in V);print('draftSharksIdp cross-market:', [s.get('is_cross_market') for s in dc._RANKING_SOURCES if s['key']=='draftSharksIdp'])"
reproduction.expected: the fit sources appear among the IDP-curve-routed sources
reproduction.actual: IDP-curve-routed: ['dlfIdp','dlfRookieIdp','idpShow','fantasyProsIdp'] · idpTradeCalc value-direct: True · draftSharksIdp cross-market: [True]

userImpact: Four expert IDP rank lists are converted to values by a curve fit to two retail calculators that are priced by a completely different mechanism. No measurement anywhere establishes that the shapes match, and the same 2026-07-29 promotion moved this curve by up to −34.6% (W04-F003).

priorFinding.note: Reproduced exactly against the live registry and the live _curve_for_source routing.

whatWorks: _curve_for_source is a three-line, unambiguous routing function and the hillCurves contract block stamps routed:false on the unrouted ROOKIE master honestly.
rootCause: Fit scopes are named for a source's SUBJECT MATTER (offense/IDP/rookie) while routing is decided by is_cross_market and _VALUE_BASED_SOURCES membership. The two taxonomies were never reconciled.
requiredRepair: Fit each master from the sources that _curve_for_source actually routes to it. For the IDP master that set publishes no values, so the honest options are to route IDP-scope rank-signal sources through the OFFENSE master (the constants are already close) or to derive the IDP curve from the board's own realized IDP rank→value relation.

title: `model_registry.py validate` decides promotion by comparing criteria recorded on different snapshot dates — the exact unpaired comparison promotion.py's docstring says invalidates the verdict
claimUnderTest: promotion.py module docstring: 'the comparison is always made on ONE snapshot with both curves scored against it… A rule that compared this week's challenger to last week's champion SCORE would be reading five days of market drift as model quality.'
observed: cmd_validate reads champ.holdout['criterion'] and challenger.holdout['criterion'] straight out of the registry JSON and feeds both to decide_promotion. Those two numbers were recorded on different days against different scrapes of the four holdout CSVs. Champion v2's criterion is stamped 2026-07-28; challenger v3's is stamped 2026-08-04. Running `validate 3` today prints improvement +12.8; the paired comparison of the same two parameter sets on today's boards is +22.3, and the registry's own v3 note (written by the PAIRED driver) records +22.4. The CLI is off by 9.6 points against a 25-point margin whose stated noise floor is ~1.5 points.

reproduction.command: cd /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket && .venv/bin/python scripts/model_registry.py validate 3 && .venv/bin/python -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from src.model_registry.holdout import evaluate_offense_master as e;a=e(0.11,1.11).criterion;b=e(0.108,1.11).criterion;print('paired improvement today: %+.2f' % (a-b))"
reproduction.expected: the CLI's improvement equals the paired improvement
reproduction.actual: CLI: 'improvement +12.8 does not clear the 25-point margin'; paired today: +22.25

userImpact: No user-visible number today — both paths reject v3. But the operator-facing decision tool disagrees with the automated driver by 6.3x the noise the margin was sized against, so it can reject a genuine improvement or promote a non-improvement, and the operator has no signal that the two disagree. `status` compounds it by printing three criteria from three dates in one comparable-looking column.

priorFinding.note: Reproduced by running the CLI and the paired evaluation side by side; the prior finding asserts the defect but not the 9.5-point live magnitude.

whatWorks: auto_refit_hill_curves.py, the automated path, DOES score both curves on one snapshot and is correct. promotion.decide_promotion itself is a clean, well-documented function.
rootCause: decide_promotion takes two scalars and cannot tell whether they came from one snapshot; the CLI is the caller that supplies mismatched ones.
requiredRepair: cmd_validate must re-score the champion's params via evaluate_offense_master before comparing, exactly as the driver does. Stored per-version criteria should be labelled with the snapshot fingerprint they were measured on and never compared across rows.

title: No recorded holdout criterion is reproducible: the boards it scores are overwritten every scrape and archived for only 3 of 21 sources, so champion v2's 787.84 recomputes to 753.05 today
claimUnderTest: versioning.py: 'Without the fingerprints "version 7" is a label; with them it is reproducible.' The registry is built around provenance and stores trainingInputs sha256 for every version.
observed: The fingerprints record WHICH bytes a version was fitted on but the bytes themselves are not kept. CSVs/site_raw/*.csv is rewritten in place by every scrape; exports/archive/*.zip (129 snapshots, 2026-07-14 → 08-04) bundles site_raw for exactly three sources — ktc, ktcSfTep, idpTradeCalc — and NONE of the four holdout boards. data/raw/ holds dated snapshots for 22 sources but is frozen at 2026-04-03→04-08 and contains no directory for otcffb, pfkDynasty or fantasyNavigator at all. Re-running evaluate_offense_master with each version's own params today reproduces none of the three recorded criteria: v1 819.73→791.68, v2 787.84→753.05, v3 775.05→730.80. The champion's drift alone (−34.79) is 139% of the 25-point promotion margin. Recomputed fingerprints match the recorded ones for only 2 of 6 training inputs.

reproduction.command: cd /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket && .venv/bin/python -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from src.model_registry.versioning import ModelRegistry;from src.model_registry.holdout import evaluate_offense_master as e;r=ModelRegistry.load('hill_scope_masters');[print(v.version,v.status,'recorded',v.holdout['criterion'],'today',round(e(v.holdout['params']['c'],v.holdout['params']['s']).criterion,4)) for v in r.versions]"
reproduction.expected: recorded criterion == recomputed criterion for every version
reproduction.actual: 1 retired recorded 819.7335 today 791.6826 / 2 champion recorded 787.8416 today 753.0495 / 3 rejected recorded 775.0471 today 730.8023

userImpact: No historical claim about the value model can be checked. An operator cannot verify that the champion ever earned its promotion, cannot diagnose a suspect verdict, and cannot roll a decision back to the evidence behind it — while `status` prints the stale number as the champion's standing score.

priorFinding.note: Prior claims stability sweeps are irreproducible because retention prunes inputs. Confirmed and extended to the promotion gate itself, with the exact recorded-vs-recomputed table.

whatWorks: fingerprint_inputs is correct and does record 'missing' rather than omitting an absent input, so a version fitted on five sources is distinguishable from one fitted on six.
rootCause: Provenance was implemented as hashes without a content store. Nothing archives the holdout CSVs, and the one archive that exists (exports/archive) was scoped to the three scraper-native boards.
requiredRepair: Archive all 21 site_raw CSVs alongside each registry write (they are small — the current 24 total ~1 MB) and record the archive path on the ModelVersion. Until then, stop rendering per-version criteria in one column in `status`.

title: A holdout board silently lost 24% of its rows in one day and the gate scored it anyway — that one board's shrinkage accounts for 99.3% of the criterion's drift
claimUnderTest: holdout.py: 'The fit truncates every source to its top 400 before computing percentiles. Matched exactly so train and holdout RMSE are the same quantity measured on different data.' MIN_ROWS_FOR_SCORING = 100 is the only depth guard.
observed: CSVs/site_raw/otcffbSf.csv went from 454 priced rows at commit 891d1600 (2026-08-03) to 347 at f320e560 (2026-08-04) — a 23.6% collapse in one day, against a registry-declared depth of 460. Because 347 > MIN_ROWS_FOR_SCORING, the gate scores it anyway; because _percentile_pairs uses i/(n−1), the percentile coordinate of every row changes with n, so the SAME curve now scores 853.52 where it scored 991.68. Decomposing the champion's criterion drift: FantasyCalc +1.08, FantasyNavigator 0.00, PFKDynasty −2.09, OTCFFB −138.16 — divided by four, OTCFFB contributes −34.54 of the −34.79 total. No warning, no skip, no note in the registry.

reproduction.command: cd /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket && git show 891d1600:CSVs/site_raw/otcffbSf.csv | wc -l && wc -l < CSVs/site_raw/otcffbSf.csv && .venv/bin/python -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from src.model_registry.holdout import evaluate_offense_master as e;r=e(0.11,1.11).to_dict();print(r['perSourceRows'],r['perSource'])"

numericProof.formula: (853.5235 − 991.6813) / 4 = OTCFFB's share of the mean-per-source criterion drift

userImpact: Twofold. (1) A source-side outage moves the promotion criterion by more than the entire promotion margin, so the next weekly gate can promote or reject on a scrape failure rather than on curve quality. (2) otcffbSf still declares depth=460 in _RANKING_SOURCES, so _expected_sources_for_position expects it down to rank ~575 while it now stops at 347 — every offense row between those ranks is silently one vote thinner than the coverage audit believes.

priorFinding.note: Not in the prior index. Detectable only by re-running the gate against today's tree.

whatWorks: holdout.py DOES record perSourceRows on every result, which is what made this visible at all. It also refuses outright when no board can be scored.
rootCause: MIN_ROWS_FOR_SCORING=100 guards against an empty board but not against a board that shrank relative to its own history. There is no comparison against the previous run's row counts.
requiredRepair: Skip (or alarm on) a holdout board whose priced-row count moved more than a few percent since the last recorded run — perSourceRows is already persisted, so the comparison is free. Separately, reconcile otcffbSf's declared depth with reality.

title: Every tuned constant in the core blend was selected against a day-to-day board-churn metric the repo's own report calls 'product-bad'; none was ever tuned against accuracy
claimUnderTest: reports/backtest_blend_params.md: 'Lower = more stable = probably better-calibrated.' Six committed reports present recommendations in the vocabulary of validation ('Promote α = 0.00', 'The design-choice justification … is empirically validated').
observed: Every backtest in reports/ optimizes mean absolute change in canonicalConsensusRank across consecutive-day pairs. Per constant: α shrinkage — stability; report recommends α=0.00, production ships 0.10, and the joint report states plainly that the stability optimum is 'use the anchor source alone, ignore the 15 other sources… That's product-bad'. MAD λ — stability; report recommends 0.0, production ships 0.0, so the one constant that matched its report is the one that switched the stage off. _PERCENTILE_REFERENCE_N — stability; report recommends N=400, production ships 500, and the script's own header calls the metric 'degenerate for this particular question' because a smaller N flattens more of the board and therefore has less left to churn ('a maximally uninformative board can win'). Soft fallback — stability; recommends distance=0.00. Coverage weight (MIN_FULL_COVERAGE_DEPTH=60) — no backtest of any kind exists; docs/measurements/coverage-weight-impact-2026-07-29.json measures its IMPACT after the fact, not its correctness. No accuracy target exists anywhere in this path: the repo has no forward-looking outcome join for the market board.

reproduction.command: cd /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket && grep -n 'product-bad' reports/alpha_lambda_joint_backtest_full.md && grep -n 'Promote' reports/alpha_shrinkage_backtest_full.md reports/percentile_reference_n_backtest_full.md && .venv/bin/python -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'.');import src.api.data_contract as dc;print('live alpha',dc._ALPHA_SHRINKAGE,'live N',dc._PERCENTILE_REFERENCE_N,'live lambda',dc._MAD_PENALTY_LAMBDA)"
reproduction.expected: live constants trace to an accuracy measurement
reproduction.actual: joint report line 9 contains 'That's product-bad'; alpha report says 'Promote α = 0.00' vs live 0.1; N report says 'Promote N=400' vs live 500; every objective is mean absolute rank change

numericProof.formula: count(constants whose shipped value equals its report's recommendation)

userImpact: Every value on /rankings and every trade verdict rests on a parameter set chosen to minimize how much the board moves day to day. That objective is maximized by discarding sources, is known-degenerate for N, and is unrelated to whether a player is priced correctly. Three of five constants do not even match the recommendation their own report produced, with no note anywhere saying why.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed with the verbatim 'product-bad' quote and the per-constant shipped-vs-recommended table. Also confirms PRIOR-A09-F08 (N ships 500 against its own 400 recommendation) and PRIOR-A24-F10.

whatWorks: The scripts themselves are honest instruments and reproducible; backtest_percentile_reference_n.py in particular states its own degeneracy in the module docstring and prints it into new reports. λ=0.0 was correctly acted on and the MAD stage is genuinely inert.
rootCause: No ground-truth target for dynasty asset value exists in this repository for the market board, so stability was adopted as a proxy and then read as if it were the target.
requiredRepair: Either build a realized-outcome target for the market board (the machinery exists — src/model_registry/board_holdout.py + compute_player_season_scores already do exactly this for the adjusted-board test) and re-derive the constants, or rewrite every report to state that its recommendation is a churn preference and not evidence about the constant's value.

title: No historical record of the served board exists — archived exports carry the raw scraper composite only, so every 'historical' backtest blends today's 18 source CSVs into a weeks-old payload
claimUnderTest: reports/alpha_shrinkage_backtest_full.md: 'Snapshot count: 25, Date range: 2026-03-23 → 2026-04-16'. player_valuation.py: 'The fit is structurally stable — 16 archived snapshots spanning 2026-07-16 → 07-30 returned offense midpoint 65.4… against rankDerivedValue on the served board.'
observed: An archived export's player rows contain _composite, _finalAdjusted, _rawComposite, _canonicalSiteValues and three site columns. They contain NO rankDerivedValue, NO canonicalConsensusRank, NO confidenceBucket, NO sourceRanks — the entire canonical blend output is absent. Every backtest therefore RECONSTRUCTS a board by calling build_api_data_contract(old_payload), and that function reads the CSV-backed sources from CSVs/site_raw/ at the paths hardcoded in _RANKING_SOURCES — from disk, today, not from the snapshot. userImpact: Nothing about the value model can be validated historically, and the repo's docs claim otherwise in at least four places: the α/λ/N/soft-fallback reports ('Snapshot count: 25 · Date range …'), player_valuation.py's 'served board' stability note, docs/legacy-rank-curve-backtest.md, and CLAUDE.md's description of the refit gate. Per section 39: because no historical source snapshots exist for 18 of 21 sources, NO model in this repository may be described as validated. The splits are not rolling or expanding — there are no splits, only consecutive-day pairs of reconstructions.

priorFinding.note: Confirms PRIOR-A13-F13 ('no temporal validation exists anywhere in the calibration path') and PRIOR-A24-F10/F11. The repo has independently measured the same 21/18 split inside backtest_percentile_reference_n.py; this reproduces it and extends it to the missing rankDerivedValue in the archive, which that note does not cover.

whatWorks: src/model_registry/board_holdout.py is the one honest exception: it scores against realized 2025 points under the league's exact rules, uses a seeded paired bootstrap, and its docstring states outright that the forecast claim 'would need board snapshots taken before a season that this repo does not keep'. docs/adjusted-board-backtest.md reports 'no difference detected' rather than claiming a win.
rootCause: The export format was designed as a scraper artifact and predates the canonical blend; nobody extended it when rankDerivedValue became the product's value. build_api_data_contract reads CSV paths from module constants, so it has no way to be pointed at a snapshot.
requiredRepair: (1) Write playersArray (or at minimum rankDerivedValue + canonicalConsensusRank + confidenceBucket + sourceRanks) into every export. (2) Archive all 21 site_raw CSVs per snapshot. (3) Give build_api_data_contract an optional site_raw root so a replay reads the snapshot's own CSVs. Until (1)-(3) land, no backtest in reports/ should be cited as evidence.

title: The temporal-leakage caveat is present in 1 of 9 backtest scripts and 0 of 7 committed reports — every report a reader would actually open presents its recommendation unqualified
claimUnderTest: backtest_percentile_reference_n.py: 'Both caveats are now printed in the generated report, next to the recommendation, so a reader cannot take "promote N=1000" as an accuracy finding.'

title: 'Confidence' on the board is one unvalidated agreement bucket, not separate calibrated dimensions, and it never shrinks a value — it only reorders and filters
claimUnderTest: Section 40 asks whether the separate confidence dimensions are real and calibrated, and whether low confidence shrinks a claimed edge. methodology.confidenceBuckets presents high/medium/low/none as a graded quality reading.
observed: _compute_confidence_bucket takes exactly two inputs — sourceCount and sourceRankPercentileSpread — and thresholds them at 0.08/0.20. That is one dimension (source agreement about ORDER), and it is agreement about rank, not about the value it labels. No other dimension feeds it: _marketConfidence and identityConfidence exist on the same row and are unrelated quantities that never combine into it. No calibration measurement of any kind exists in the repo: nothing tests whether a 'high' row is more accurate, more stable, or narrower in any realized sense than a 'low' row. On the live board 448 of 1,092 rows (41.0%) are 'low' and only 113 (10.3%) are 'high'. Downstream, confidence never scales a value: suggestions.py adds a flat +2/+1/0 to a rank_score (reordering only, and off its own sourceCount thresholds of 6/3, which disagree with the contract's rule), and edge-helpers.js uses the bucket only as an include/exclude filter. The single value-shrinking mechanism in the pipeline is the single-source haircut, which keys on sourceCount==1, not on confidence — so a five-source row with a 0.5 percentile spread is labelled 'low' and its value is used at full face in every trade calculation.

userImpact: A user sees a 'Low confidence' badge next to a value that the trade calculator, the arbitrage finder, the waiver bidder and the terminal all use at 100% weight. The badge implies the number is softer; the arithmetic downstream treats it as hard. 41% of the board is in that state.

priorFinding.note: Prior finds three unrelated quantities ship under the word 'confidence'. Confirmed (confidenceBucket / _marketConfidence / identityConfidence coexist unmerged) and extended with the section-40 question the prior does not answer: no calibration exists and no value is shrunk. Also overlaps PRIOR-A12-F04.

whatWorks: The percentile-spread signal is the right choice over the absolute-ordinal one (it makes small IDP pools comparable to large offense pools), the fallback rule is documented as not-the-live-path, and quarantined rows are correctly degraded to 'low'.
rootCause: confidenceBucket was built as a display badge and never given a decision-theoretic role, so nothing forced it to be calibrated or to have an effect.
requiredRepair: Either (a) measure it — the archive supports a forward test of |Δvalue| by bucket once W04-F009 is fixed — and make low confidence shrink the value used by the engines, or (b) rename it to what it is ('source agreement') and stop rendering it in a vocabulary that implies uncertainty about the price.

title: src/backtesting/harness.py has no production caller, and the only 'correctness' it defines is agreement with a future reading of the same board
